summary: Provisioning stalls on office VLAN when corporate TLS inspection breaks Intune/Autopilot enrollment
description:
Issue summary: New Windows devices stuck in OOBE/Autopilot provisioning on the corporate office VLAN. Impact: Multiple new hires (approx. 6 devices) could not complete Intune enrollment; delays to productivity and Device Inventory accuracy. Environment: prod:us-west office VLAN (VLAN 210), devices on wired Ethernet; affected images are standard corporate Autopilot image (Win11-Redwood-Base v3.2).

Observed behavior: During OOBE the device reaches 'Applying your settings' then shows 'Can't connect right now' or loops back to sign-in. Intune/Enrollment logs show repeated TLS handshake errors and HTTP failures when contacting management endpoints.

Expected behavior: Device should complete Autopilot flow, register in Azure AD, and appear in Intune with expected config profiles and applications.

Attachments/links: see network capture link and SRE dashboard links in investigation notes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Connect a freshly imaged laptop to office wired network (VLAN 210) and boot into OOBE.
2) Proceed through Autopilot until Intune enrollment step attempts to contact management endpoints.
3) Observe error or stall at 'Applying your settings' and eventual OOBE failure/loop.
4) Repeat same image on corporate guest Wi-Fi or home network — provisioning succeeds (used to isolate network).
logs: MDM enrollment logs: Registration failed: 0x80180014 / HTTP 400 during token exchange
Event viewer (DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics-Provider): 0x801C001A TLS handshake failed: unexpected certificate subject
Browser-level capture during OOBE: TLS alert (handshake_failure) against https://enterpriseregistration.windows.net/ and https://login.microsoftonline.com/
Tcpdump (office VLAN): observed TLS client hello followed by RST from inline proxy appliance; packet length truncated on large POST payloads (~>16KB)
investigation_notes: 03/10 11:20 Support triage: confirmed issue reproduced on VLAN 210; devices on other subnets unaffected.

03/10 13:05 SRE captured PCAPs during OOBE — identified inline TLS inspection appliance (Corp-Proxy-SSL) replacing certs for login.microsoftonline.com; chain does not include necessary EKU for device auth, Intune token exchange fails.

03/10 15:40 Network team (J. Morales) verified corporate TLS inspection appliance is performing MITM but is configured to exempt some SaaS endpoints; currently management endpoints were not in exempt list.

03/11 09:30 Observed that split-VPN config on new laptops (default corporate VPN client) attempts to establish a VPN session very early in OOBE and some routes are pushed that make device traffic flow through an additional inline gateway that truncates large POSTs. Combined with TLS inspection, token payloads are corrupted causing enrollment failures.

03/11 11:00 Workaround test: added temporary bypass (no TLS inspect) for login.microsoftonline.com, enterpriseregistration.windows.net, manage.microsoft.com, and MDM endpoints for VLAN 210. Re-ran provisioning on 3 devices — all completed successfully.
03/11 14:20 Correlation with prior ticket INT-62100 (intune dynamic group propagation) — different scope but referenced for enrollment flakiness patterns.
resolution: Temporary fix: Network applied an emergency change to bypass TLS interception for Microsoft identity and Intune-related endpoints for VLAN 210; provisioning verified on previously blocked devices. Permanent action: Change request submitted to Network change board to add a permanent exemption list for Autopilot/Intune endpoints across corporate inspection appliance and to confirm no packet truncation for large POSTs. Follow-ups: Update onboarding runbook to include recommended VPN split-tunnel preconfiguration and document exemption list for future Office VLANs. Close after change window and monitoring (owner: network-team).
